parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReceivingService is in the business (domain) layer. Most of what it does is business logic. receive() checks that the quantity is a positive whole number and calls Bin.put, which does the capacity and weight logic. pick() spreads a pick across the bins and asks Item.needsReorder whether to reorder. The service runs these use cases, loading data from the table classes and storing it back through them. It writes no SQL, opens no connections, runs no transactions and uses no storage framework itself, so the actual persistence work stays in src/persistence. It also has no transport or framework concerns such as HTTP, requests or serialization formats. The layer model is a classic three-tier stack (presentation → business → persistence), and in that model a business service that calls table gateways is doing its intended job. Whether business may depend on persistence is an import-direction question, which is out of scope here. The only borderline part is the private item() and bin() helpers, which turn table rows into domain objects field by field, and the `{ ...bin }` record passed to store(). That is light data-mapper glue, so I did not count it as a separate persistence responsibility. If repositories were moved behind domain ports, this mapping would belong in persistence.
